_comment: The English catalogue, and the template for every other language.
Copy this file to <code>.json (a BCP 47 code: fr, pt-BR, zh-Hans) and
translate the values. Keys are never translated. See locales/README.md.

tiles._comment: The captions rendered into tile artwork. Keep them short: a tile is 600px wide and a long name shrinks until it fits.

names._comment: The names of the entries written into apps.json. The #1 and Zz prefixes are sort keys, not decoration -- see the README -- so keep them.

ui._comment: The interface. Anything shown to a person belongs here.

scanning.heading: Scanning your libraries
scanning.elapsed: {seconds}s elapsed. Steam is quick; Heroic reads its whole library and takes the longest.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.nothing_touches_your_list: None of this touches your app list.
settings.appearance_why: Following the system is the default. On a television, where there is no system to follow, pick the one that suits the room.
settings.updates_why: Checked only when you ask. Nothing is downloaded or installed without you saying so.
settings.offer_development_builds_why: Newer, and sometimes broken. Off means only finished releases.
settings.move_to_finished_release: Move to the finished release when it is newer
settings.move_to_finished_release_why: A release is where a development build was heading, so this leaves you on the finished one rather than stranded on an older preview. Only applies while development builds are on.

report.scan_this_why: There is no way to type a web address into a stream, so here it is as a code. It goes to the issues page for this program.
report.report_a_bug_why: This opens the issues page in your usual browser. The manager stays open behind it.
report.or_scan_it: Or scan it with your phone
